verses.text: Now these are the kings of the land, whom the children of Israel struck, and possessed their land beyond the Jordan toward the sunrise, from the valley of the Arnon to Mount Hermon, and all the Arabah eastward:

Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon, and ruled from Aroer, which is on the edge of the valley of the Arnon, and the middle of the valley, and half Gilead, even to the river Jabbok, the border of the children of Ammon;
and the Arabah to the sea of Chinneroth, eastward, and to the sea of the Arabah, even the Salt Sea, eastward, the way to Beth Jeshimoth; and on the south, under the slopes of Pisgah:
and the border of Og king of Bashan, of the remnant of the Rephaim, who lived at Ashtaroth and at Edrei,
and ruled in Mount Hermon, and in Salecah, and in all Bashan, to the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and half Gilead, the border of Sihon king of Heshbon.
Moses the servant of Yahweh and the children of Israel struck them. Moses the servant of Yahweh gave it for a possession to the Reubenites, and the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.

These are the kings of the land whom Joshua and the children of Israel struck beyond the Jordan westward, from Baal Gad in the valley of Lebanon even to Mount Halak, that goes up to Seir. Joshua gave it to the tribes of Israel for a possession according to their divisions;

in the hill country, and in the lowland, and in the Arabah, and in the slopes, and in the wilderness, and in the South; the Hittite, the Amorite, and the Canaanite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite:
the king of Jericho, one; the king of Ai, which is beside Bethel, one;
the king of Jerusalem, one; the king of Hebron, one;
the king of Jarmuth, one; the king of Lachish, one;
the king of Eglon, one; the king of Gezer, one;
the king of Debir, one; the king of Geder, one;
the king of Hormah, one; the king of Arad, one;
the king of Libnah, one; the king of Adullam, one;
the king of Makkedah, one; the king of Bethel, one;
the king of Tappuah, one; the king of Hepher, one;
the king of Aphek, one; the king of Lassharon, one;
the king of Madon, one; the king of Hazor, one;
the king of Shimron Meron, one; the king of Achshaph, one;
the king of Taanach, one; the king of Megiddo, one;
the king of Kedesh, one; the king of Jokneam in Carmel, one;
the king of Dor in the height of Dor, one; the king of Goiim in Gilgal, one;
the king of Tirzah, one: all the kings thirty-one.

footnotes.content: These names—Sihon, Og, and all the rest—are more than a roster for a history book. Each king represents a stronghold the Lord broke through so His people could inherit. When I see a long list like this, I'm reminded that victory isn't just one grand triumph; it's faithful step after faithful step.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo in this accounting: the Lord's faithfulness isn't faint or theoretical. It's as solid as these ancient stones, these named kings, these conquered territories. What He promises, He performs—and we can trust Him with the territories of our own lives.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Sihon ruled from Aroer to the Jabbok, commanding the middle of the Arnon valley. This wasn't mere geography; these boundaries marked real dominion that stood until the Lord gave Israel passage and victory. The precision of the text honors both the land and the people who fought for it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: From the Salt Sea eastward—the Lord led them through terrain both beautiful and harsh. Chinneroth, the Arabah, Beth Jeshimoth—each place a waypost of His faithfulness. He didn't just give the victory; He gave them a land He had already prepared.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Og of Bashan, one of the Rephaim—a giant among the remaining old powers. Yet he fell too. There's something tender about how God's Word records even the strong ones who stood against Him, not to mock them but to show that no stronghold stands forever except His.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Mount Hermon, Salecah, the reach of Og's kingdom—the Lord gave it all. When I read these ancient borders and place names, I'm struck by how the Lord doesn't just win battles; He grants territories, homes, and futures to His people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Moses struck these kings; now Joshua records it. Two generations, one faithfulness. The Reubenites, Gadites, and half of Manasseh received what was promised long before—a reminder that God's word, spoken generations ago, ripens into real inheritance.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Joshua and the children of Israel struck them westward—from Lebanon to Seir. Here begins the roster of the western conquest, land He gave them according to their divisions. Each tribe received their portion, a token of how personally the Lord knows His own.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hill country, lowland, Arabah, slopes, wilderness, South—the Lord gave them such varied terrain! Not just victory, but a rich inheritance of different lands for different tribes. There's beauty in imagining how each people settled into their corner of the promised land.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jericho and Ai—names that echo with meaning. Jericho's walls fell by faith; Ai was where Israel learned obedience. Now they're recorded here as conquered, part of the promised land. Sometimes the hardest victories become the sweetest memories.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jerusalem and Hebron—great cities in their day. Jerusalem would become David's city; Hebron was where the patriarchs walked. The Lord gave both to His people, fulfilling promises spoken centuries before Abraham's grandchildren were born.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jarmuth, Lachish—more names, more victories. Each one required courage, faith, and the Lord's strength. When I read through a list like this, I'm reminded that faithfulness isn't glamorous; it's steady, piece by piece, trust by trust.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Eglon and Gezer—two more kings whose dominions passed away. What seemed immovable in their day crumbled when the Lord acted. It's a quiet lesson for any who fear what stands against them today.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Debir and Geder—the list goes on, each name a proof of the Lord's faithfulness. I marvel at how carefully the text records each one, honoring the work of conquest and the Lord's provision.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hormah and Arad—places where Israel had to learn hard lessons and fight hard battles. Now they stand as conquered cities in the promised land. Even our struggles become part of our inheritance when the Lord leads us through them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Libnah and Adullam—more names, more victories. I notice how thoroughly the text records them, as if to say: none of these conquests were overlooked or forgotten by the Lord. Every single one mattered.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Makkedah and Bethel—Bethel, that place where Jacob once dreamed of a ladder to heaven. Now it falls to Joshua's Israel. The Lord's promises stretch across generations and transform the very landscape.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Tappuah and Hepher—two more strongholds that gave way. Each entry in this list is proof that the Lord keeps His covenant word. He said He would give the land; He did, city by city, king by king.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Aphek and Lassharon—as I read these names from a distant age, I'm struck by the solidity of the Lord's work. Cities and kingdoms rose and fell, but His purpose held firm, and His people inherited what He promised.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Madon and Hazor—Hazor was a great city, yet it fell. The Lord showed that no fortress, no matter how mighty, stands when His purpose advances. It's a comfort to those who feel outmatched by the powers around them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Shimron Meron and Achshaph—the names grow less familiar, but each one is real, each one counts. The Lord's meticulous record reminds me that no faithful work goes unnoticed, no territory conquered by His people goes unrecorded.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Taanach and Megiddo—places that would echo through later history, yet they fell to Joshua's generation. The Lord's hand moved through their time as it moves through ours, step by faithful step.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Kedesh and Jokneam in Carmel—more cities, more victories, each one part of the vast, faithful provision of the promised land. I'm grateful for how the text honors them all, great and small alike.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Dor and Goiim in Gilgal—even the smaller kingdoms fell to the Lord's people. There's no hierarchy of importance in His sight; every victory belongs to Him, every territory gained is part of His faithfulness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Tirzah—the last name, the thirty-first king. A complete accounting, a full roster of conquered kingdoms. The Lord's work was thorough, His promise fulfilled completely. What a wonder to read it all recorded here: every promise kept.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
